title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: DENISE'S SISTER
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Denise, a city bus driver in Portland, Oregon.
Eight years ago, she had a fight with her little sister Lori. About a piano.
They haven't spoken since. Not one word.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE MAGNET
segments.quote: The most difficult thing is the decision to act. The rest is merely tenacity.
segments.author: Amelia Earhart
lines: One night, Denise found an old photo. Two girls in matching sweaters, laughing.
She picked up the phone. Then she put it down. Three times.
On her fridge was a magnet Lori gave her years ago, with words from the pilot Amelia Earhart:
The most difficult thing is the decision to act. The rest is merely tenacity.
Denise dialed. It went to voicemail. She left the worst message of her life. But she left it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE POSTCARDS
segments.quote: The only way to have a friend is to be one.
segments.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
lines: No call back. Weeks went by.
Mr. Gus, a regular rider on her bus, saw her face and quoted Ralph Waldo Emerson:
The only way to have a friend is to be one.
So every Friday, Denise mailed Lori a postcard. No speeches. Just a joke, and a hello.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE LETTER
segments.quote: The weak can never forgive. Forgiveness is the attribute of the strong.
segments.author: Mahatma Gandhi
lines: On card number nine, Lori finally wrote back. Two pages. All about what Denise did wrong.
Denise grabbed a pen to fire back. Then she remembered Gandhi:
The weak can never forgive. Forgiveness is the attribute of the strong.
So she wrote just three words. I'm sorry, Lori.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE PHONE CALL
segments.quote: Don't look back. Something might be gaining on you.
segments.author: Satchel Paige
lines: That Sunday, Lori called. They talked for an hour, and tried hard not to argue about the piano.
Denise wanted to go over every old detail. Then she thought of baseball legend Satchel Paige:
Don't look back. Something might be gaining on you.
So she asked, Want to come for Thanksgiving?

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE GRAVY
segments.quote: The art of being wise is the art of knowing what to overlook.
segments.author: William James
lines: Lori came. She hugged Denise, then tasted the gravy and said, Mom made it better.
Old Denise would have thrown the gravy boat.
New Denise remembered a line from the thinker William James:
The art of being wise is the art of knowing what to overlook.
She laughed, and said, Mom made everything better. Pass the rolls.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE PIANO
segments.quote: Darkness cannot drive out darkness; only light can do that. Hate cannot drive out hate; only love can do that.
segments.author: Martin Luther King Jr.
lines: After pie, Lori admitted something. She can't even play the piano. Neither can Denise.
They laughed until they cried. Then Lori read a card she'd brought, with words from Doctor Martin Luther King Junior:
Darkness cannot drive out darkness; only light can do that. Hate cannot drive out hate; only love can do that.
Now they talk every Sunday. And the piano? It's a very expensive shelf for family photos.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Make the call. Show up. Forgive. Look ahead. Let it go. Choose love.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Make the call. Keep showing up. Forgive first. Look ahead. Let the small stuff go. And choose love.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night. And call your sister. Mine says I still owe her twenty dollars.
